tasks.title: HANDOFF: Hostinger KVM1→KVM2 (8 GB) upgrade
tasks.notes: Scheduled for today. Steps: quiesce writers → backup 6 app DBs → hPanel snapshot + click Upgrade → health check. Keep engine at 1500 MiB after upgrade.

prep.what: Run the Hostinger VPS upgrade from KVM1 to KVM2 (8 GB RAM) for the Takeoff Engine server.
prep.understand: This is a live server migration with a precise order of operations. The backup script (`backup_azteam_vps.py`) isolates all 6 app DBs with off-host hashes for a safe isolated restore. After the upgrade, the engine must stay at 1500 MiB limit until the Linux corpus proof at 4 GiB/3200 MiB passes separately. The free-plan branch (`cost/engine-free-plan-20261104`, commit 010570e) ships only after that proof.
approach: Read `.orc/reports/takeoff-engine-engine-cost-20261104-221300-upgrade-handoff.md` and `tools/ops/README.md` (commit 930cabe) end-to-end before touching anything.
Quiesce writers, then run: `python3 tools/ops/backup_azteam_vps.py --execute --quiesced` — backs up 6 app DBs with isolated restore verification and off-host hashes.
Take the hPanel snapshot and click the KVM2 Upgrade in Hostinger's control panel.
Run `check_azteam_vps.py` health check to confirm all services are up; verify engine is still at 1500 MiB limit.

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Rooms show 'unnamed' on PDFTron plans because all text is outlined — the live-text lane finds nothing. M3 tiles lane proven in spike (run_labels_m3tiles.py, ~4.3 min/sheet). MINIMAX_AI key must reach the VPS. Add callout-vs-room filtering for Holabird noise.

prep.what: Productize the M3 tiles vision lane as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action, and add callout-vs-room noise filtering.
prep.understand: PDFTron outlines ALL text on some firm plans (the famous probe finding — 55 live words, zero room labels found on Harborview). The M3 tiles lane (spike `run_labels_m3tiles.py`) reads labels from rasterized tiles using the MINIMAX_AI vision model at ~4.3 min/sheet. Holabird confirms the lane works: 92/109 rooms named in PROD. The noise problem is R13-documented: general-note paragraphs, UP stair arrows, and FEC callouts all match as room names. The §7a metered-credits event gates credit consumption. MINIMAX_AI key must be in VPS secrets.
approach: Productize `run_labels_m3tiles.py` as an opt-in 'read labels (AI)' action triggered from the UI (button, not auto-run — it costs credits).
Wire the §7a metered-credits event so each invocation charges the correct credit amount.
Confirm MINIMAX_AI key is reachable from the VPS (the key must reach the VPS per existing decision); if not, add it to the secrets config.
Add callout-vs-room filtering: exclude general-note paragraphs, UP stair arrows, and FEC callouts from room-name candidates using R13 patterns.

prep.what: Finish the assemblies-per-room engine: wire room-type classification into the CSI library to produce paint, drywall, flooring quantities, and wall heights per room.
prep.understand: This is PRD Phase 1 / Pillar 3. The scaffold is in `engine/assemblies.py` (folded into B1). The pattern: classified room type → CSI library formulas → up to 8 quantities per room. Example: 'bathroom' → wall sqft (paint), wall panels (drywall), floor sqft (flooring), 8-ft wall height. The room classifier (t6, done) feeds this. This is the last pillar before estimator-grade Excel output.

Map each room type to its CSI library formulas: at minimum paint (wall sqft), drywall (wall + ceiling panels), flooring (floor sqft), wall height (type-specific default).
Wire the classifier output into assemblies.py and produce a quantities dict per room.
Add a round-trip test: classified room → assemblies dict → verify output quantities match a known room spec.

prep.understand: Door recall blocks the SEAL_FT global seal relax. The localseal coverage guard (t15) made this safe: bad chords now self-revert instead of merging rooms. Implement raster-gap detection for door recall as a replacement for the failed symbol-based approach.
Test bi-fold / cased-opening patterns against the dental GT set where scallop detection works.
Re-run the 12-judge GT corpus scorer and confirm chord coverage improvement above 0.3+ on the target sets.

tasks.title: Performance hardening — target 100 on every page, desktop + mobile
tasks.notes: Structural work already done (3,209-byte app.js, self-hosted fonts, fetchpriority=high heroes, CLS structurally zero, no third-party embeds). Remaining: run Lighthouse per route, fix what actually fails. Likely culprit: shared-hosting TTFB on cold PHP.

prep.what: Run Lighthouse across the site's key pages and fix any performance failures — the structural foundation is already in place, this is measure-then-fix.
prep.understand: The heavy structural work is done: `app.js` ships at 3,209 bytes with no React preload, fonts are self-hosted woff2 via `bunny()` with metric-adjusted fallbacks (zero third-party origins), heroes use `fetchpriority=high` as real `` elements, CLS is structurally zero (width+height from build manifest), and all three heavy third-party embeds are gone. The likely remaining issue is TTFB on cold PHP (shared hosting). Fix path: `php artisan optimize` (route/view/config caching) first, then full-page HTML cache if TTFB is still the blocker.
approach: Run Lighthouse CLI or Chrome DevTools against: home page, a service page, and one town page — both mobile (Lighthouse 'mobile' preset) and desktop.
Record the actual failing metrics and their scores (don't guess — measure first).
If TTFB > 600ms: run `php artisan optimize` on the host (or confirm it already runs in the deploy script) to enable route/view/config caching.
Re-run Lighthouse after the cache fix and confirm the score improves; iterate until 100 on the tested pages.
resources: Laravel `php artisan optimize` (route cache + view cache + config cache)
deploy/deploy-ssh.sh — check if optimize already runs at deploy time
